correctness.rationale: Using Bézout against both lines, any other integral plane curve of degree d>=2 satisfies −K.C=3d−Σα−Σβ>=d and by adjunction C²>=d−2>=0. The only negative curves are exceptional E_i,F_j, marked-line transforms A,B with squares 1−n,1−m, and cross-block secants L_ij of square −1. Distinct cross L_ij intersect 1 iff both indices differ; a pairwise-compatible family of bipartite edges must therefore be empty, singleton, or a star. Selected exceptional curves cannot share endpoints with selected L. Schur complement for selected A,B with k,ℓ eligible exceptionals gives [[−(n−1−k),1],[1,−(m−1−ℓ)]], negative definite iff k<=n−2, ℓ<=m−2, excluding k=n−2 AND ℓ=m−2. The four marked line choices yield exactly P_ab; summing star footprints produces the theorem. Independently expanded all coefficients for (3,3): total 1092 and last coefficient 37; (3,4): (1,21,150,529,1047,1170,638,92), total 3648; (4,4): 11925, maximal 209. The universal result is by the negative-curve and graph proof, not finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Only two proper collinear blocks with line intersection not among centers; no extra infinitely-near or three-line patterns.
Finite independent checks cover (3,3),(3,4),(4,4), while the all-parameter classification is proved algebraically.
